prediction: THREE SMALL CHANGES IN gl/, and the prediction is that NONE of them moves a capture. Registered precisely because that is the interesting outcome to be wrong about. (1) THE OFF-BY-ONE. gl/texture.c hand-rolls the surface-overlap test that decides which surfaces to write back before a texture is read from guest memory: 'tex_vram_end = texture_vram_offset + length - 1', 'surf_vram_end = surface->vram_addr + surface->size - 1', then 'overlapping = !(surface->vram_addr >= tex_vram_end || texture_vram_offset >= surf_vram_end)'. Both ends are INCLUSIVE and both comparisons are '>=', which is the exclusive-end form. For inclusive ends the test must be '>' on both sides, so as written it reports NOT overlapping for two ranges that overlap in exactly one byte at either boundary -- the surface's last byte being the texture's first, or the texture's last being the surface's first. gl/surface.c's own check_surface_overlaps_range() gets this right with exclusive ends and '>=', and pgraph_gl_download_surfaces_in_range_if_dirty() -- added this session for the blit range download -- wraps exactly this loop. The change replaces the hand-rolled loop with that call, which fixes the boundary case and removes the duplicate predicate.
